yes it's an easter egg

Let's not talk about anything else, let's talk about Huawei's waterproofing. Last time my Huawei fell into the Mariana Trench, I thought the phone was definitely done for - either water would get in or the water pressure would burst it. What I never expected was that my Huawei used its Leica lens as eyes, automatically turned on the flashlight to light up the seafloor, used the phone's GPS as navigation, relied on the streamlined feel of the metal body, and kept paddling with the phone's vibration, and actually found me again! The warmth radiating from the Kirin 8-core CPU meant that when I got my Huawei back it wasn't cold to the touch, but slightly warm. At that moment, I truly felt the warmth of the motherland. I entered the great Huawei in this life, and in the next I'll still be Chinese. Next let's talk about Huawei's flash. Now I don't even wear a headlamp when I go mining - as soon as I take out my phone, the whole mine lights up. The signal is super strong. I remember one time our mine flooded and collapsed, over 6000 meters underground, and none of the 500+ coworkers' phones had signal. I took out my Huawei and made the emergency call. And Huawei's battery is awesome. When the rescue workers found us, the power had gone out due to the collapse, and they used ropes to pull up over 200 people. But suddenly a secondary collapse happened, and if we didn't rescue people quickly, it would all be over. I took the battery out of my Huawei and hooked up the elevator, and suddenly the whole mine had power. The elevator roared - before, it could only pull 10 people at a time, but with a Huawei battery it pulled over 50, and in 5 minutes everyone was rescued. After saving everyone, they gave me the battery back; after putting it back in it was still at 98%.
Are you sure you want to quit?
